clue.text: My soldiers must restrict free passage

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so the earlier words close around the next one

parts.note: cor! is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
OR, other ranks, the ordinary soldiers
to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

explanation.surface: An exclamation that troops must block somebody's right of way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive, but it is the British exclamation of surprise, like 'gosh'; 'free' is the verb, as in ridding a house of mice.
explanation.definitionFit: A corridor is a long hallway or narrow strip of land through which people move, which is what a passage is.

clue.text: Curse abrupt chap's way of behaving

indicators.note: abrupt means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: cuss is an informal word for curse
Tom is a stock man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: Swearing as a curt fellow's habitual manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a habitual practice or usual way of acting, typical of a person or society.

clue.text: What almost half of us wanted to do on the ocean

definitions.text: What almost half of us wanted to do

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in letter headings
the main is a poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: Nearly half the people wanted to be out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In the 2016 UK referendum on EU membership, 48% voted to stay in the EU, the side called Remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Remain was the losing referendum option in 2016, backed by just under half of British voters.

clue.text: I often can't go out when I want

definitions.text: I often can't go out when I want

parts.words: I often can't go out when I want
parts.note: surface reading: someone stuck at home, unable to leave the house
setter's reading: go out means lose consciousness, so this person struggles to fall asleep

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out' suggests a social outing, but it means drop off like a light going out.
explanation.definitionFit: An insomniac is someone who habitually cannot sleep, lying awake at night despite wanting rest.

clue.text: Poem the vicar reworked is too forceful

indicators.note: reworked material is redone in a new form, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman's verse, once revised, comes across as too strident.
explanation.definitionFit: Overemphatic means stressing something more strongly than necessary, being excessively insistent in tone.

clue.text: A female in dress on which animals may be seen

definitions.text: on which animals may be seen

indicators.note: something in a dress is wrapped by it, so the first pieces sit inside the garment

parts.note: a sari is the draped dress worn in South Asia
F is the standard abbreviation for female
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman in a frock, perhaps patterned with animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description of the dress's print, but it describes the holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an expedition, usually in Africa, made specifically to watch or photograph wild creatures in their habitat.

clue.text: Actor in rep

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who acts or brings about an effect
second meaning: a representative acting on behalf of someone else

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a performer in repertory theatre; rep is the theatre company in the surface, a representative in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an active cause of change and a person who represents others in business.

clue.text: Fellow about to be saved by a trained medic

indicators.note: something saved by another is held safe inside it, so the abbreviation goes within
something trained is shaped and disciplined, so the letters are put into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged
ca is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A man rescued by a qualified doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Fellow suggests a man, but it is a university fellow, a member of a college's teaching staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow of a university college is a senior scholar, so an academic in the crossword sense.

clue.text: What model says he's doing at work in August

definitions.text: What model says he's doing at work

definitions.meaning: second meaning: grand, stately, impressive in appearance

explanation.walkthrough: August looks like the summer month, but it is the adjective meaning majestic.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing describes something grand and impressive in size or bearing, as august does.

clue.text: Term of high esteem Spanish dude embraces

indicators.note: an embrace wraps arms round someone, so the title goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: Sr is the abbreviation for señor, the Spanish for mister

indicators.note: high can mean intoxicated, and a drunken word staggers into a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: A season of admiration, with a Spanish gentleman giving someone a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High esteem' reads as a single phrase, but high is the signal to rearrange the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is one half of a university or school year, the period the word term also names.

clue.text: Leave, as a drag queen might do after a gig?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to depart suddenly or secretly

definitions.text: as a drag queen might do after a gig?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read playfully: to remove the flamboyant theatrical style worn on stage

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the word as DE-CAMP: camp is the exaggerated theatrical style, and a performer sheds it once the show ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart in a hurry, and the punning reading strips away camp flamboyance after performing.

clue.text: Royal Academy member wins MP's constituency

parts.note: to win something is to gain it
a borough is a town that historically returned its own Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: A painter gets elected for a parliamentary seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gainsborough, the 18th-century portrait and landscape painter, was a founding member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsborough was one of the original members of London's Royal Academy when it was founded in 1768.

clue.text: A number of poppies?

parts.note: surface reading: a count of red flowers, as in a field
setter's reading: a number is something that numbs, a narcotic obtained from the poppy plant

explanation.walkthrough: Number is read as 'numb-er', a thing that numbs; the drug from poppy sap is the classic painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is the narcotic drug extracted from the seed pods of the opium poppy, used to deaden pain.

clue.text: Insist upon head showing precision

parts.note: to exact is to demand or insist upon payment
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's Scottish place names

explanation.surface: Demanding a leader who displays accuracy.
explanation.walkthrough: Head here is a promontory, not a boss or a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness is the quality of being accurate and correct in every detail, a close synonym of precision.

clue.text: Pianist done playing without soprano's permission

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the rearranged letters sit around the singer
playing suggests the notes are performed freely, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
S is the standard abbreviation for soprano in choral music

explanation.surface: A pianist finishes a performance without needing the singer's go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' usually means lacking, which suggests removing a letter; here it is the older sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispensation is an official exemption or licence granted by an authority, so it amounts to formal permission.

clue.text: A chap carrying on with English male in Deal

indicators.note: a man carrying a load holds it within his grasp, so the later letters go inside

parts.note: taken as written
gent is short for gentleman, a chap
re means on or about
E is the abbreviation for English
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man keeps going with an Englishman in Deal, the Kent seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is capitalised to look like the Kent town; 'carrying on' is split so on becomes a contained piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal is an arrangement reached between parties, which is what an agreement is.

clue.text: Had to go after a Pole, one walking away from party?

parts.note: taken as written
a pole is an upright post
had dinner means ate it

explanation.surface: Somebody ate following a Polish guest, then left the gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Pole is capitalised to suggest a person from Poland; it is a stake. The party is a political or religious one.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a religious faith or political cause, deserting the party they once belonged to.

clue.text: Don't go and overlook marriage, they said

definitions.note: a verb phrase for a noun: a mismatch is two things that don't go together

indicators.note: what people said is heard rather than read, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to overlook something is to miss it
a match is a marriage, as in a good match

explanation.surface: Gossips advising someone to skip a wedding they would rather ignore.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, 'miss match' gives the single word with one S.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that don't go together, like clashing colours or an ill-suited couple, form an incompatible pairing.

clue.text: Royal once tangled up in printer cable

indicators.note: a tangled cable is twisted out of order, so these letters come in a muddled sequence

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A historical royal caught up in the leads of a printer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's husband, a royal consort who died in 1861, hence 'once'.

clue.text: Stop at home, having got in some Bass

indicators.note: having got something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a bass is one kind of fish
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Staying in after stocking up on Bass, the English beer brand.
explanation.walkthrough: Bass is capitalised to suggest the beer; a bass is also a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish is to bring something to an end, so it means to stop.

clue.text: Artist about to put on brew for one holding cup?

indicators.note: here on is taken as into, so that piece is put inside the drink

parts.note: beer is a brew

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, a crossword stock artist

explanation.surface: A painter about to make tea for whoever carries a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cup suggests a trophy or teacup; a bearer is anyone carrying something, such as the cup bearer at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearer is a person who carries something, so a cupbearer is one holding a cup.

clue.text: Smile more after tickling a steward of Burgundy?

indicators.note: tickling makes someone squirm and wriggle, so the letters are jiggled into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Grinning wider once a nobleman's servant is tickled.
explanation.walkthrough: Burgundy suggests the old French duchy and its court officials, but it is the wine, so the steward serves it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sommelier is a restaurant's wine waiter, who looks after and serves wines such as red Burgundy.

clue.text: Use a rubber with Times puzzle ultimately

parts.note: eras are periods of time

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of puzzle

explanation.surface: Getting the eraser out when finishing the newspaper crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: Times is capitalised to suggest the newspaper; a rubber is the British word for an eraser.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out pencil marks, which is what you do when you use a rubber.

clue.text: Cream cake finally containing few calories

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, so only its closing letter is used

parts.note: the closing letter of cake
lite is the product-label spelling of light, meaning low in calories

explanation.surface: A cream cake that is, in the end, low in calories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Containing' looks like an insertion signal, but it belongs to the phrase that means LITE.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its best members, the select few, which is what an elite is.

clue.text: Like flipping large paintings of stars

parts.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'

indicators.note: flipping turns something over end to end, so the following letters run backwards

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: Someone who loves big canvases depicting the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' reads as a verb of enjoying but is the word AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral is the adjective for things relating to or coming from the stars, as in astral bodies.

clue.text: Snooty boss

definitions.meaning: first meaning: haughty, looking down on others
second meaning: a person of higher rank at work, or the head of a religious house

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a stuck-up manager, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for a condescending attitude and a noun for someone ranking above you.

clue.text: Reminders for key tasks Republican leader ignored

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: something ignored is left out of account, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: chores are routine household tasks

indicators.note: a leader goes at the front, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of the party name

explanation.surface: Memos about important jobs that the party chief never bothered with.
explanation.walkthrough: Key is a musical key here, not 'important'.
explanation.definitionFit: Echoes of the past are traces that recall it, so they act as reminders of earlier things.

clue.text: Time one devises a plot to snare politician

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time in physics

parts.words: one devises a plot to snare
parts.note: to hatch a plot is to devise it, so a schemer is a hatcher

explanation.surface: A schemer's plan to catch a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was Britain's Conservative prime minister from 1979 to 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was a famous British politician, so the surname works as an example of one.
